     1	[![CI - main](https://github.com/dalito/ucumvert/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/dalito/ucumvert/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

     3	
     4	# Easier access to UCUM from Python
     5	
     6	> **Feedback welcome!**
     7	> Currently only the conversion direction from UCM to pint is supported.
     8	> Please review the definitions before you trust them.
     9	> While we have many tests in place and reviewed the mappings carefully, bugs may still be present.
    10	
    11	[UCUM](https://ucum.org/) (Unified Code for Units of Measure) is a code system intended to cover all units of measures.
    12	It provides a formalism to express units in an unambiguous way suitable for electronic communication.
    13	Note that UCUM does not provide a canonical representation, e.g. `m/s` and `m.s-1` are expressing the same unit in two ways.
    14	
    15	**ucumvert** is a pip-installable Python package. Features:
    16	
    17	- Parser for UCUM unit strings that implements the full grammar.
    18	- Converter for creating [pint](https://pypi.org/project/pint/) units from UCUM unit strings.
    19	- A pint unit definition file [pint_ucum_defs.txt](https://github.com/dalito/ucumvert/blob/main/src/ucumvert/pint_ucum_defs.txt) that extends pint´s default units with UCUM units. All UCUM units from the new version 2.2 of the specification (June 2024) are included.
    20	
    21	**ucumvert** generates the UCUM grammar by filling a template with unit codes, prefixes etc. from the official [ucum-essence.xml](https://github.com/ucum-org/ucum/blob/main/ucum-essence.xml) file (a copy is included in this repo).
    22	So updating the parser for new UCUM releases is straight forward.
    23	The parser is built with the great [lark](https://pypi.org/project/lark/) parser toolkit.
    24	The generated lark grammar file for case-sensitive UCUM codes is included in the repository, see [ucum_grammar.lark](https://github.com/dalito/ucumvert/blob/main/src/ucumvert/ucum_grammar.lark).
    25	
    26	Some of the UCUM unit atoms are invalid unit names in pint, for example `cal_[15]`, `m[H2O]`, `10*`, `[in_i'H2O]`.
    27	For all of them we define mappings to valid pint unit names in [ucum_pint.py](https://github.com/dalito/ucumvert/blob/main/src/ucumvert/ucum_pint.py), e.g. `{"cal_[15]": "cal_15"}`.
    28	
    29	## Install
    30	
    31	ucumvert is available as Python package from [PyPi](https://pypi.org/project/ucumvert) and can be pip-installed in the usual way.
    32	
    33	```bash
    34	pip install ucumvert
    35	```
    36	
    37	To install the most recent code from git in developer mode including creation of a virtual environment use:
    38	
    39	Linux
    40	
    41	```bash
    42	git clone https://github.com/dalito/ucumvert.git
    43	cd ucumvert
    44	python -m venv .venv
    45	source .venv/bin/activate
    46	python -m pip install --upgrade pip
    47	pip install -e .[dev]
    48	```
    49	
    50	Windows
    51	
    52	```bash
    53	git clone https://github.com/dalito/ucumvert.git
    54	cd ucumvert
    55	py -m venv .venv
    56	.venv\Scripts\activate.bat
    57	py -m pip install --upgrade pip
    58	pip install -e .[dev]
    59	```
    60	
    61	Optionally you can visualize the parse trees with [Graphviz](https://www.graphviz.org/) as shown below. It requires the additional package [pydot](https://pypi.org/project/pydot/); install by running `pip install pydot`.
    62	
    63	## Demo
    64	
    65	We provide a basic command line interface.
    66	
    67	```cmd
    68	(.venv) $ ucumvert
    69	```
    70	
    71	It has an interactive mode to test parsing UCUM codes:
    72	
    73	```cmd
    74	(.venv) $ ucumvert -i
    75	Enter UCUM unit code to parse, or 'q' to quit.
    76	> m/s2.kg
    77	Created visualization of parse tree (parse_tree.png).
    78	main_term
    79	  term
    80	    term
    81	      simple_unit       m
    82	      /
    83	      annotatable
    84	        simple_unit     s
    85	        2
    86	    .
    87	    simple_unit
    88	      k
    89	      g
    90	--> Pint <Quantity(1.0, 'kilogram * meter / second ** 2')>
    91	> q
    92	```
    93	
    94	So the intermediate result is a tree which is then traversed to convert the elements to pint quantities (or pint-compatible strings):
    95	
    96	![parse tree kg*m*s**-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dalito/ucumvert/main/parse_tree.png)
    97	
    98	The package includes an UCUM-aware pint UnitRegistry which loads all definitions for UCUM units on instantiation.
    99	It comes with an additional method `from_ucum` to convert UCUM codes to pint.
   100	
   101	```python
   102	>>> from ucumvert import PintUcumRegistry
   103	>>> ureg = PintUcumRegistry()
   104	>>> ureg.from_ucum("m/s2.kg")
   105	<Quantity(1.0, 'kilogram * meter / second ** 2')>
   106	>>> ureg.from_ucum("m[H2O]{35Cel}")  # UCUM code with annotation
   107	<Quantity(1, 'm_H2O')>
   108	>>> _.to("mbar")
   109	<Quantity(98.0665, 'millibar')>
   110	>>> ureg("degC")   # a standard pint unit
   111	<Quantity(1, 'degree_Celsius')>
   112	>>>
   113	```
